text.en: Raju saw iron turn red-brown after weeks in the rain. "That is a chemical reaction called rusting," said his teacher.

Chemical reactions are of several types. In a combination reaction two or more substances form one product, in decomposition one substance breaks into simpler ones, in displacement a more reactive element replaces a less reactive one and in double displacement two compounds exchange ions. Reactions are also classed as reversible or irreversible.
The rate of a chemical reaction is how fast the reactants change into products and depends on concentration, temperature, pressure, surface area and catalysts. In a reversible reaction the system reaches a state of equilibrium when the forward and backward rates are equal.
The ionic product of water leads to the pH scale, pH = -log of the hydrogen ion concentration, with 7 neutral, below 7 acidic and above 7 basic for dilute aqueous solutions near 25 °C. pH matters in everyday life, such as in the stomach, in teeth and in soil.
Chemical reactions are of several types.

In a combination reaction two or more substances form one product, in decomposition one substance breaks into simpler ones, in displacement a more reactive element replaces a less reactive one and in double displacement two compounds exchange ions.
Reactions are also classed as reversible or irreversible.
The rate of a chemical reaction is how fast the reactants change into products and depends on concentration, temperature, pressure, surface area and catalysts.
In a reversible reaction the system reaches a state of equilibrium when the forward and backward rates are equal.
The pH scale measures acidity. At about twenty-five degrees Celsius, neutral water has pH seven. A lower pH is acidic and a higher pH is basic.
pH matters in everyday life, such as in the stomach, in teeth and in soil.
A chemical reaction changes which atoms are connected. In a physical change such as melting ice, the substance remains water.

board.text: A new substance is evidence of chemical change

text.en: A colour change or a new solid can suggest a reaction. Bubbles can also come from boiling, so one observation by itself may not prove a chemical change.
Count atoms of each element before and after a reaction. Ordinary chemical reactions rearrange atoms without making or destroying them.
Put numbers before formulas to match the atom counts. Changing a subscript would change the substance represented by the formula.
In the textbook equation for carbon and oxygen forming carbon dioxide, there is one product type. We can read the pattern without doing the reaction.

board.text: Combination joins reactants into one product

text.en: A diagram with one compound on the left and two new substances on the right shows the decomposition pattern.

board.text: Decomposition goes from one reactant to multiple products

text.en: In a simplified model, metal A replaces metal B in a compound if A can displace B under those conditions.
In an ion model, two compounds can exchange their partners. A reaction may produce an insoluble solid or form water.
When dissolved ions bond into an insoluble substance, a solid can separate. That new solid is called a precipitate.

board.text: A precipitate is an insoluble solid formed in solution

text.en: An acid and a base can form water and a salt. The final pH depends on the starting substances and how much of each is present.

board.text: Neutralisation can make salt and water

text.en: An exothermic reaction gives energy to its surroundings. An endothermic process takes in energy from its surroundings.
Compare how much product forms in the same time. The trial producing more in that interval has the higher average rate.

board.text: Rate describes change per unit time

text.en: More reacting particles in the same space can cause more collisions each second. This often increases the rate.
At higher temperature, particles usually move faster. More collisions can then have enough energy for reaction.

board.text: Warming can make more collisions effective

text.en: For the same amount of solid, many small pieces provide more exposed surface than one large piece. This can help a surface reaction occur faster.

board.text: Smaller pieces can expose more surface

text.en: A catalyst can make a reaction faster without being used up overall. Catalase in living tissue is one familiar example.

board.text: A catalyst provides another reaction pathway

text.en: A reversible reaction has both a forward direction and a reverse direction. Each can occur if the appropriate particles are present.
At equilibrium, the two directions continue. The amounts stay steady because the forward and reverse rates match.
A mixture may contain more reactant than product at equilibrium. What matches is the rate at which the two directions occur.

board.text: Equal rates do not mean equal amounts

text.en: For dilute aqueous solutions, lowering pH from six to five means about ten times greater hydrogen-ion concentration.

board.text: One pH unit means a factor of ten

text.en: Lemon juice is acidic. The stomach also has an acidic environment. Its pH is one example of why acidity matters in living things.
Some plants suit more acidic soils and others grow better nearer neutral. Test results can help compare conditions for a crop.

board.text: Soil pH affects which plants grow well

text.en: First notice the reactant and product pattern. Then use a separate idea such as energy, rate, equilibrium or pH to explain another feature of the change.

problem.en: What is the pH of a neutral aqueous solution at about 25 °C?

text.en: pH is a scale from 0 to 14.
Pure water is neutral.
Its pH is 7.

problem.en: Why is melting ice not a chemical reaction?

text.en: The solid becomes a liquid.
The substance remains water.

why.en: There is no new chemical product.

problem.en: In a model, AB and CD form AD and CB. Which reaction pattern is this?

text.en: Each product contains a part from each reactant.
This is double displacement.

why.en: Two compounds form two differently paired compounds.

problem.en: Compare hydrogen-ion concentration in dilute solutions of pH 5 and pH 7.

text.en: Their pH readings differ by two units.

why.en: Each unit represents a factor of ten.

text.en: The pH 5 solution has about 100 times higher hydrogen-ion concentration.

prompt.en: A friend says A pH of 3 means the solution is basic. How will you reply?

points.en: Rate depends on concentration, temperature and more.
Equilibrium has equal forward and backward rates.
For dilute aqueous solutions near 25 °C, pH 7 is neutral.
